queries: FrontierMath OpenAI verbal agreement not to train Epoch AI holdout
LMArena Meta Llama 4 Maverick experimental version policy update leaderboard

sources_considered.why: Primary source. It shows OpenAI open-sourced SimpleQA, questions and answers included, and evaluates its own models on it.
Reputable report quoting Epoch AI leaders. OpenAI's promise not to train on FrontierMath was only a verbal agreement, and Epoch could not independently verify OpenAI's score.
Quotes LMArena's statement on the Llama 4 episode. This was after the post, so it is context only.

receipt.public_excerpt: We hope that open-sourcing SimpleQA drives the research on more trustworthy and reliable AI forward

evidence_items.explanation: The SimpleQA questions and answers are open to anyone, including the vendors who report scores on it. Nothing described here stops a vendor from tuning on the answers, so honest results depend on trust.

receipt.public_excerpt: while OpenAI has access to FrontierMath, it has a “verbal agreement” with Epoch AI not to use FrontierMath’s problem set to train its AI.

evidence_items.explanation: For a leading math benchmark, the only safeguard against OpenAI training on test problems it could see was a verbal agreement. That is an honor system with no formal enforcement.

receipt.public_excerpt: “However, we can’t vouch for them until our independent evaluation is complete.”

evidence_items.explanation: The benchmark's own lead mathematician said OpenAI's reported score rested on trust and had not been independently verified. This matches Zitron's point that outsiders can't easily tell whether a vendor cheated.

receipt.public_excerpt: Meta should have made it clearer that “Llama-4-Maverick-03-26-Experimental” was a customized model to optimize for human preference. As a result of that we are updating our leaderboard policies

evidence_items.explanation: After the post, a vendor's leaderboard entry was publicly challenged. The response was a public statement and a policy update, not a formal penalty. This falls outside the target period, so it is context only.

unresolved_gaps: Whether reputational damage counts as a 'real consequence' is a matter of judgment.
The maxim that honor systems 'often don't work' at high stakes is not scored.
